query: For high-value components operating in aggressive environments, what intervention could improve surface physical and mechanical characteristics? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should remain effective, prior evidence that would support it, and an experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying an AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film via co‐filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (Co‐FCVAD), followed by an optimized annealing process, will enhance the surface hardness, oxidation resistance, and tribocorrosion performance of high‐value components in aggressive environments.
generation.material_initial_state: Metallic components that currently have untreated or conventionally treated surfaces, which are susceptible to wear, oxidation, and degradation under high-temperature and corrosive conditions.
generation.intervention: Deposit an AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film using Co‐FCVAD and then anneal the coated components (e.g., at 800 °C for 1 hour) to promote the formation of a dense protective oxide layer.
generation.conditions: Service environments characterized by high temperatures and corrosive media (such as high-temperature oxidation and friction-corrosion coupling conditions), similar to those simulated in relevant coating studies.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a dense composite oxide layer (e.g., containing ZrTiO4) at the surface, combined with the intrinsic lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening provided by the high-entropy alloy composition.
generation.mechanism: The synergistic interactions among the multiple principal elements in the HEA, together with the annealing-induced formation of a continuous oxide layer, lead to increased hardness and improved resistance to oxidation and wear. This oxide scale acts as a barrier against harsh environmental factors, while the HEA microstructure reinforces surface integrity.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable increase in surface hardness and enhanced tribocorrosion performance relative to untreated components, thereby extending the service life of components operating in aggressive environments.
generation.baseline: Components without the HEA coating typically exhibit lower hardness and are more vulnerable to oxidation, wear, and degradation under high temperature and corrosive conditions.
generation.boundary: The improved properties are expected under conditions similar to the experiments (high temperature around 800 °C and corrosive media typical of oxidizing environments). The effectiveness may vary with other service temperatures, environmental chemistries, or if the coating process is significantly altered.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of improvement in mechanical properties and corrosion resistance is uncertain and may depend on fine details of the film composition, deposition parameters, and annealing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of test specimens made of the same high-value component substrate: one set receiving the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film via Co-FCVAD with subsequent annealing, and a control set with an untreated surface. Subject both groups to accelerated aging in a high-temperature oxidizing and friction-corrosion environment that mimics aggressive service conditions.
measurements: Wear rate measurement (e.g., mass loss or volume loss after cyclic wear tests)
Oxidation scale integrity and thickness via XRD and SEM-EDS analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated specimens do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement (for example, less than a 10% increase) in hardness, wear resistance, or oxidation layer integrity compared with the untreated control group under identical test conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractAlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy (HEA) films with strong amorphization were obtained by co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition, and the effect of thermal shock on the films was investigated in order to explore the protection mechanism of HEA films against mechanical components in extreme service environments. The results show that after annealing at 800 °C for 1 h, the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the surface actively prevents the oxidation from continuing, so that the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film exhibits excellent oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air. In the friction-corrosion coupling environment, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film annealed at 800 °C for 1 h shows the best tribocorrosion resistance due to the stable dense microstructure and excellent mechanical properties, and its ΔOCP, COF and wear rate possess the smallest values of 0.055, 0.04 and 1.34 × 10−6 mm−3·N−1·m−1.Keywords: AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film, thermal shock, oxidation, tribocorrosion

Filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (FCVAD) has sufficient advantages to obtain multi-component films due to its characteristics of magnetic filtration, high ionization rate (100%) and controllable ion types and ion energy. Co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (Co-FCVAD) is obtained by designing a multi-channel for particle transport based on FCVAD, which significantly improves the defects of uncontrollable composition and poor quality in the preparation of HEA films [,]. Thus, in order to improve the performance of mechanical components in extreme service environments, the AlCrTiZrMo film system is determined by selecting elements with a large atomic radius difference and excellent corrosion and high temperature performance. In this work, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film is prepared based on Co-FCVAD. The synergistic interaction between elements at a high temperature in air is discussed, and the changes in microstructure, mechanical properties and tribocorrosion properties of the film after annealing at different temperatures are studied, so as to analyze the protection mechanisms of AlCrTiZrMo HEA films in the simulated scenario of thermal shock.
